title: Configurationally Locked Ridaifen-B Analogs as Potent Ebola Virus Entry Inhibitors.
abstract: In the face of emerging outbreaks, high mortality rates, and limited treatment options, Ebola virus (EBOV) disease poses a global public health threat, underscoring the need for effective therapies. The unique and critical role that EBOV glycoprotein (GP) plays in the viral life cycle makes it an attractive target for antiviral drug discovery. In this study, we report on the design, synthesis, and evaluation of a series of cyclized ridaifen-B-based inhibitors with enhanced antiviral activity and selectivity against EBOV. Several compounds exhibited nanomolar potency inhibiting EBOV-GP-mediated entry and submicromolar potency against Marburg virus entry. Site-directed mutagenesis indicated inhibitor binding at the EBOV GP1/GP2 fusion loop. The compounds displayed favorable in vitro pharmacokinetic parameters, which encouraged testing the in vivo rapid PK for hit compound 41. This study highlights the potential of 1,2-dihydronaphthalene and tetrahydronaphthalene derivatives as valuable leads for the development of potent antifiloviral agents targeting EBOV among other filoviruses.

analysis.summary_en: This study addresses the critical need for effective therapies against Ebola virus disease, a global public health threat characterized by high mortality and limited treatment options. The researchers focused on the EBOV glycoprotein (GP), a key component of the viral life cycle, as a target for antiviral drug discovery. They designed, synthesized, and evaluated a series of cyclized ridaifen-B-based inhibitors. title: Evidence for a detection ceiling in the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease epidemic in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: an analysis of publicly reported aggregate surveillance data
abstract: The 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) epidemic in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) was declared on 15 May 2026 and determined a public health emergency of international concern on 17 May 2026. Public surveillance reporting consists of cumulative counts by report date; no line list with symptom-onset dates is available. Widely circulated characterisations - that this is the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak on record, that reported cases are doubling every 22 days, and that the case fatality ratio (CFR) is 37.5% - rest on these aggregates. We examined what the published data actually support. We assembled twelve published anchor points from 15 May to 13 July 2026 from WHO, WHO AFRO, NICD and the DRC National Institute of Public Health; one was recovered by back-calculation and checked against the directly reported subsequent total. We computed mean daily incidence between anchors and the within-interval death-to-case ratio. We reconstructed symptom-onset dates by Richardson-Lucy deconvolution with right-truncation correction under assumed onset-to-report delays with means of 5, 7 and 9 days, estimated the instantaneous reproduction number using the Cori method, and computed three CFR estimators: crude, resolved-case and outcome-delay-adjusted. Provincial CFRs used exact binomial intervals. Confirmed cases plateaued at 40-52 per day for eighteen days, from 25 June to 13 July. Over the same period, the within-interval death-to-case ratio rose from 0.28 to 0.58. Reconstructed Rt was 1.28, with a 95% credible interval of 1.15-1.41, on 7 July, having fallen from approximately 2.9 in mid-May. Growth on the reconstructed onset curve corresponded to a doubling time of approximately 90 days, compared with 22 days computed from cumulative counts. CFR estimates were 37.5% for the crude estimator, 50.2% for the outcome-delay-adjusted estimator and 67.3% for the resolved-case estimator. Crude provincial CFR was 34.9% with a 95% confidence interval of 32.7-37.1 in Ituri, 58.2% with a 95% confidence interval of 50.7-65.5 in North Kivu, and 81.0% with a 95% confidence interval of 58.1-94.6 in newly affected provinces. A flat case count accompanied by a rising death-to-case ratio is difficult to reconcile with a transmission plateau and is consistent with saturated case detection. Reported case counts appear to have substantially decoupled from transmission and cannot presently distinguish control from detection failure. Doubling times computed from cumulative totals are artefacts. Test volume and positivity by health zone are the critical missing denominators.

elements_en.research_question_and_background: The 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease epidemic in the Democratic Republic of the Congo was declared a public health emergency of international concern, but widely circulated characterisations of its growth and severity rest on aggregate surveillance data that may not accurately reflect the underlying transmission dynamics.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: The study analysed publicly reported aggregate surveillance data from 15 May to 13 July 2026, assembling twelve anchor points from WHO, WHO AFRO, NICD and the DRC National Institute of Public Health.
elements_en.methods: The authors reconstructed symptom-onset dates using Richardson-Lucy deconvolution with right-truncation correction, estimated the instantaneous reproduction number using the Cori method, and computed three case fatality ratio estimators: crude, resolved-case and outcome-delay-adjusted.
elements_en.main_results: Confirmed cases plateaued at 40-52 per day for eighteen days, the within-interval death-to-case ratio rose from 0.28 to 0.58, the reconstructed reproduction number was 1.28 (95% credible interval 1.15-1.41) on 7 July, and provincial case fatality ratios were 34.9% (32.7-37.1) in Ituri, 58.2% (50.7-65.5) in North Kivu, and 81.0% (58.1-94.6) in newly affected provinces.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the decoupling of reported case counts from transmission as evidence of a detection ceiling, contrasting the 22-day doubling time from cumulative counts with a 90-day doubling time from reconstructed onset dates.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that reported case counts cannot presently distinguish control from detection failure and highlight the critical need for test volume and positivity data by health zone to accurately assess epidemic control.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on publicly reported aggregate surveillance data without line lists, which limits the ability to reconstruct precise onset dates and introduces uncertainty; the evidence strength is assessed as moderate due to these data limitations and the reliance on back-calculated anchor points.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 2026 年刚果民主共和国发生的本迪布焦病毒病疫情被宣布为国际关注的突发公共卫生事件,但广泛流传的其增长和严重程度特征依赖于 监测 汇总数据,这些数据可能无法准确反映 传播 的基本动态。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究分析了 2026 年 5 月 15 日至 7 月 13 日公开报告的 监测 汇总数据,汇集了来自 WHO、WHO AFRO、NICD 和刚果国家公共卫生研究所的 12 个锚点。
elements_zh.methods: 作者使用带有右截断校正的 Richardson-Lucy 反卷积重建了症状发作日期,使用 Cori 方法估计了瞬时繁殖数,并计算了三种病死率估计量:粗略的、已解决的病例和结果延迟调整的。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将报告病例数与 传播 的脱钩解释为检测上限的证据,将累积计数的 22 天倍增时间与重建的发病日期的 90 天倍增时间进行了对比。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,报告的病例数目前无法区分控制与检测失败,并强调卫生区迫切需要检测量和阳性数据,以准确评估流行病控制。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究依赖于公开报告的汇总 监测 数据,但没有行列表,这限制了重建精确发病日期的能力并引入了不确定性;由于这些数据限制以及对反算锚点的依赖,证据强度被评估为中等。

title_zh: 刚果民主共和国 2026 年本迪布焦病毒病疫情检测上限的证据:对公开报告的 监测 汇总数据的分析
source_body_en: The 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) epidemic in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) was declared on 15 May 2026 and determined a public health emergency of international concern on 17 May 2026. Public surveillance reporting consists of cumulative counts by report date; no line list with symptom-onset dates is available. Widely circulated characterisations - that this is the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak on record, that reported cases are doubling every 22 days, and that the case fatality ratio (CFR) is 37.5% - rest on these aggregates. We examined what the published data actually support. We assembled twelve published anchor points from 15 May to 13 July 2026 from WHO, WHO AFRO, NICD and the DRC National Institute of Public Health; one was recovered by back-calculation and checked against the directly reported subsequent total. We computed mean daily incidence between anchors and the within-interval death-to-case ratio. We reconstructed symptom-onset dates by Richardson-Lucy deconvolution with right-truncation correction under assumed onset-to-report delays with means of 5, 7 and 9 days, estimated the instantaneous reproduction number using the Cori method, and computed three CFR estimators: crude, resolved-case and outcome-delay-adjusted. Provincial CFRs used exact binomial intervals. Confirmed cases plateaued at 40-52 per day for eighteen days, from 25 June to 13 July. Over the same period, the within-interval death-to-case ratio rose from 0.28 to 0.58. Reconstructed Rt was 1.28, with a 95% credible interval of 1.15-1.41, on 7 July, having fallen from approximately 2.9 in mid-May. Growth on the reconstructed onset curve corresponded to a doubling time of approximately 90 days, compared with 22 days computed from cumulative counts. CFR estimates were 37.5% for the crude estimator, 50.2% for the outcome-delay-adjusted estimator and 67.3% for the resolved-case estimator. Crude provincial CFR was 34.9% with a 95% confidence interval of 32.7-37.1 in Ituri, 58.2% with a 95% confidence interval of 50.7-65.5 in North Kivu, and 81.0% with a 95% confidence interval of 58.1-94.6 in newly affected provinces. A flat case count accompanied by a rising death-to-case ratio is difficult to reconcile with a transmission plateau and is consistent with saturated case detection. Reported case counts appear to have substantially decoupled from transmission and cannot presently distinguish control from detection failure. Doubling times computed from cumulative totals are artefacts. Test volume and positivity by health zone are the critical missing denominators.

title: Quantifying the heterogeneity and determinants of Ebola Zaire transmission during the 10th outbreak in DRC, 2018-2020.
abstract: BackgroundThe 2018-20 Ebola virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) was the countrys largest, and the second largest globally, amid armed conflict and community mistrust. Transmission heterogeneity (superspreading) is recognised in Ebola epidemics, but empirical estimates of its extent and determinants remain scarce for DRC outbreaks. We quantified transmission heterogeneity and its determinants during this outbreak. MethodsIn this retrospective observational study, we reconstructed transmission chains for confirmed and probable cases (Aug 1, 2018, to June 25, 2020) using routinely collected Ministry of Health and Medecins Sans Frontieres surveillance data. We modelled the offspring distribution with a Bayesian negative binomial framework, correcting for incomplete contact tracing, to estimate the effective reproduction number (Reff), dispersion parameter (k), and proportion of cases responsible for 80% of transmission (prop80), overall, by subgroup, and over time. Individual-level determinants were assessed with a regression extension, adjusting for covariates. FindingsAmong 3481 cases, 2008 transmission events linked 2402 (69%) individuals into 415 chains (median size 3, range 2-102). Overall Reff was 1.00 (95% CI 0.92-1.08) with k 0.29 (0.26-0.32); 17.8% of cases generated 80% of transmission. Overdispersion stayed stable despite fluctuating Reff. Non-isolation (IRR 1.79), death outside a treatment centre (IRR 4.34), and unfollowed contact status (IRR up to 4.48) predicted more secondary cases; vaccination cut transmission by about 60%. InterpretationEpidemiological investigations linked 67.7% (2356/3481) of cases into 415 transmission chains (median size 3, range 2-102); linkage to a known infector fell to 10% during the November 2018-February 2019 period of peak insecurity. Transmission was heterogeneous overall, with dispersion parameter k of 0.29 (0.26-0.32), such that 17.8% (16.8-18.9) of cases generated 80% of onward transmission confirming superspreading as a stable, structural feature of Ebola dynamics. Critically, k remained stable throughout the outbreak, including during periods of elevated Reff, indicating that transmission surges reflected intensification of the same underlying process rather than new superspreading contexts, and that Reff alone is an insufficient summary of epidemic potential. Regression analyses identified predominantly modifiable determinants: cases not isolated in an Ebola treatment centre (IRR 1.79 [1.54-2.06]) or who died outside one (IRR 4.34 [3.47-5.31]) generated substantially more secondary cases, as did those registered as contacts but not followed up (IRR 3.01 [2.39-3.70]) or unregistered altogether (IRR 4.48 [3.67-5.38]) relative to actively followed-up contacts. Vaccination reduced onward transmission by 60-64% (IRR 0.36-0.40). These findings indicate that transmission was shaped less by gaps in epidemiological knowledge than by the operational reach of contact tracing, isolation, and vaccination delivery, particularly during periods of insecurity. FundingMedecins Sans Frontieres; Einstein-BUA Professorship, Charite - Universitatsmedizin Berlin.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究解决了 2018 年至 2020 年刚果民主共和国持续存在的埃博拉扎伊尔 传播 公共卫生问题,该地区的武装冲突和社区不信任使控制变得复杂。它的目的是量化 传播 异质性并确定其在这个大 暴发 中的决定因素。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项回顾性观察研究利用卫生部和无国界医生组织的 传播 数据,重建了 2018 年 8 月 1 日至 2020 年 6 月 25 日期间 3481 例确诊和疑似埃博拉病例的 传播 链。传播 事件将 2402 个人连接到 415 个链中。
elements_zh.methods: 重建了 传播 链,并使用贝叶斯负二项式框架对后代分布进行建模,纠正不完整的接触追踪,以估计有效繁殖数 (Reff)、分散参数 (k) 以及占 传播 80% 的病例比例。通过调整协变量的回归扩展来评估个体水平的决定因素。
elements_zh.main_results: 总体参考值为 1.00 (95% CI 0.92–1.08),k 0.29 (0.26–0.32);17.8% 的案例生成了 80% 的 传播。非隔离(IRR 1.79)、治疗 中心外的死亡(IRR 4.34)和未追踪的接触状态(IRR 高达 4.48)预测更多继发病例;疫苗接种 将 传播 削减了约 60%。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将 传播 解释为随着时间的推移是异构且稳定的,超级传播是由接触者追踪、隔离和 疫苗接种 传递方面的操作差距驱动的,而不是新的上下文。他们报告说,仅靠雷夫不足以概括流行病的潜力,并强调可改变的决定因素是控制的关键目标。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,加强接触者追踪、隔离和 疫苗接种 交付(尤其是在不安全期间)可以显着减少 传播。他们还建议 监测 应与 Reff 一起监测分散度 (k),以预测流行病的可能性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究依赖于常规 传播 数据,且接触者追踪不完整,这可能会对 传播 链和决定因素的估计产生偏差。尽管如此,贝叶斯修正和波动 Reff 的一致离散度增强了证据基础,保证了适度的置信度评估。

source_body_en: BackgroundThe 2018-20 Ebola virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) was the countrys largest, and the second largest globally, amid armed conflict and community mistrust. Transmission heterogeneity (superspreading) is recognised in Ebola epidemics, but empirical estimates of its extent and determinants remain scarce for DRC outbreaks. We quantified transmission heterogeneity and its determinants during this outbreak. MethodsIn this retrospective observational study, we reconstructed transmission chains for confirmed and probable cases (Aug 1, 2018, to June 25, 2020) using routinely collected Ministry of Health and Medecins Sans Frontieres surveillance data. We modelled the offspring distribution with a Bayesian negative binomial framework, correcting for incomplete contact tracing, to estimate the effective reproduction number (Reff), dispersion parameter (k), and proportion of cases responsible for 80% of transmission (prop80), overall, by subgroup, and over time. Individual-level determinants were assessed with a regression extension, adjusting for covariates. FindingsAmong 3481 cases, 2008 transmission events linked 2402 (69%) individuals into 415 chains (median size 3, range 2-102). Overall Reff was 1.00 (95% CI 0.92-1.08) with k 0.29 (0.26-0.32); 17.8% of cases generated 80% of transmission. Overdispersion stayed stable despite fluctuating Reff. Non-isolation (IRR 1.79), death outside a treatment centre (IRR 4.34), and unfollowed contact status (IRR up to 4.48) predicted more secondary cases; vaccination cut transmission by about 60%. InterpretationEpidemiological investigations linked 67.7% (2356/3481) of cases into 415 transmission chains (median size 3, range 2-102); linkage to a known infector fell to 10% during the November 2018-February 2019 period of peak insecurity. Transmission was heterogeneous overall, with dispersion parameter k of 0.29 (0.26-0.32), such that 17.8% (16.8-18.9) of cases generated 80% of onward transmission confirming superspreading as a stable, structural feature of Ebola dynamics. Critically, k remained stable throughout the outbreak, including during periods of elevated Reff, indicating that transmission surges reflected intensification of the same underlying process rather than new superspreading contexts, and that Reff alone is an insufficient summary of epidemic potential. Regression analyses identified predominantly modifiable determinants: cases not isolated in an Ebola treatment centre (IRR 1.79 [1.54-2.06]) or who died outside one (IRR 4.34 [3.47-5.31]) generated substantially more secondary cases, as did those registered as contacts but not followed up (IRR 3.01 [2.39-3.70]) or unregistered altogether (IRR 4.48 [3.67-5.38]) relative to actively followed-up contacts. Vaccination reduced onward transmission by 60-64% (IRR 0.36-0.40). These findings indicate that transmission was shaped less by gaps in epidemiological knowledge than by the operational reach of contact tracing, isolation, and vaccination delivery, particularly during periods of insecurity. FundingMedecins Sans Frontieres; Einstein-BUA Professorship, Charite - Universitatsmedizin Berlin.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究解决了 2018 年至 2020 年刚果民主共和国持续存在的埃博拉扎伊尔 传播 公共卫生问题,该地区的武装冲突和社区不信任使控制变得复杂。它的目的是量化 传播 异质性并确定其在这个大 暴发 中的决定因素。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项回顾性观察研究利用卫生部和无国界医生组织的 传播 数据,重建了 2018 年 8 月 1 日至 2020 年 6 月 25 日期间 3481 例确诊和疑似埃博拉病例的 传播 链。传播 事件将 2402 个人连接到 415 个链中。
analysis_zh.methods: 重建了 传播 链,并使用贝叶斯负二项式框架对后代分布进行建模,纠正不完整的接触追踪,以估计有效繁殖数 (Reff)、分散参数 (k) 以及占 传播 80% 的病例比例。通过调整协变量的回归扩展来评估个体水平的决定因素。
analysis_zh.main_results: 总体参考值为 1.00 (95% CI 0.92–1.08),k 0.29 (0.26–0.32);17.8% 的案例生成了 80% 的 传播。非隔离(IRR 1.79)、治疗 中心外的死亡(IRR 4.34)和未追踪的接触状态(IRR 高达 4.48)预测更多继发病例;疫苗接种 将 传播 削减了约 60%。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将 传播 解释为随着时间的推移是异构且稳定的,超级传播是由接触者追踪、隔离和 疫苗接种 传递方面的操作差距驱动的,而不是新的上下文。他们报告说,仅靠雷夫不足以概括流行病的潜力,并强调可改变的决定因素是控制的关键目标。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,加强接触者追踪、隔离和 疫苗接种 交付(尤其是在不安全期间)可以显着减少 传播。他们还建议 监测 应与 Reff 一起监测分散度 (k),以预测流行病的可能性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究依赖于常规 传播 数据,且接触者追踪不完整,这可能会对 传播 链和决定因素的估计产生偏差。尽管如此,贝叶斯修正和波动 Reff 的一致离散度增强了证据基础,保证了适度的置信度评估。

title: Antibody Therapy Targeting GP in Treatment of Ebola Virus Infection
abstract: Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) is a severe and acute fatal disease caused by the Orthoebolavirus zairense (Ebola virus, EBOV), first identified in 1976. From 1976 to 2025, multiple Ebola virus disease outbreaks were documented, predominantly attributable to the Zaire ebolavirus (ZEBOV) species, followed by Orthoebolavirus sudanense (Sudan ebolavirus, SUDV), with a limited number of outbreaks associated with Orthoebolavirus bundibugyoense (Bundibugyo ebolavirus, BDBV). As of 2025, numerous outbreaks caused by the EBOV have severely impacted public health and the global economy, particularly in West Africa. One of the response strategies has been the development of broad-spectrum neutralizing antibodies for prevention and treatment. ZMapp was the first antibody cocktail authorized for the emergency treatment of patients infected with ZEBOV. To date, two antibody-based therapeutics—Inmazeb and Ebanga—have been officially approved by the FDA in 2020 for the treatment of ZEBOV infection. Following the discovery of these ZEBOV-specific antibodies, numerous antibodies with broader antiviral spectra have been identified and are currently under development. This review summarizes neutralizing antibodies targeting seven key domains of the EBOV glycoprotein (GP), specifically: the glycan cap, GP1/head, base, fusion loop, GP1/core, GP1/2, and HR2/MPER (Heptad Repeat 2/Membrane-Proximal External Region). A deeper understanding of the characteristics of these neutralizing antibodies will accelerate the development of novel antibody therapies and provide guidance for the rational design of next-generation drugs against EBOV infection.

analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on the development and application of antibody therapies targeting the glycoprotein (GP) of the Ebola virus (EBOV) for the treatment of Ebola Virus Disease (EVD). The central question revolves around the efficacy and potential of these antibodies in combating EBOV infections, particularly those caused by the Zaire ebolavirus (ZEBOV) species. The review also explores the broader implications of these therapies for public health and global economies, especially in regions like West Africa that have been severely impacted by EBOV outbreaks.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review covers Ebola virus disease outbreaks from 1976 to 2025, predominantly focusing on the Zaire ebolavirus (ZEBOV) species. The review includes the development and approval of antibody-based therapeutics such as ZMapp, Inmazeb, and Ebanga, which have been authorized for the emergency treatment of ZEBOV infections. The review also discusses the identification of numerous antibodies with broader antiviral spectra that are currently under development.

title_zh: 治疗 感染中的针对 GP 的抗体治疗
source_body_en: Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) is a severe and acute fatal disease caused by the Orthoebolavirus zairense (Ebola virus, EBOV), first identified in 1976. From 1976 to 2025, multiple Ebola virus disease outbreaks were documented, predominantly attributable to the Zaire ebolavirus (ZEBOV) species, followed by Orthoebolavirus sudanense (Sudan ebolavirus, SUDV), with a limited number of outbreaks associated with Orthoebolavirus bundibugyoense (Bundibugyo ebolavirus, BDBV). As of 2025, numerous outbreaks caused by the EBOV have severely impacted public health and the global economy, particularly in West Africa. One of the response strategies has been the development of broad-spectrum neutralizing antibodies for prevention and treatment. ZMapp was the first antibody cocktail authorized for the emergency treatment of patients infected with ZEBOV. To date, two antibody-based therapeutics—Inmazeb and Ebanga—have been officially approved by the FDA in 2020 for the treatment of ZEBOV infection. Following the discovery of these ZEBOV-specific antibodies, numerous antibodies with broader antiviral spectra have been identified and are currently under development. This review summarizes neutralizing antibodies targeting seven key domains of the EBOV glycoprotein (GP), specifically: the glycan cap, GP1/head, base, fusion loop, GP1/core, GP1/2, and HR2/MPER (Heptad Repeat 2/Membrane-Proximal External Region). A deeper understanding of the characteristics of these neutralizing antibodies will accelerate the development of novel antibody therapies and provide guidance for the rational design of next-generation drugs against EBOV infection.

title: Editorial: Integrated genomic and systems approaches to unravel host-virus interactions in viral infectious diseases
abstract: Two contributions examine viruses targeting the central nervous system (CNS). A clinical and proteomic analysis of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) from 69 patients with varicella-zoster virus (VZV) CNS infection documents the predominant manifestations of headache, fever, and motor/sensory disturbances. CSF proteomics revealed markedly elevated protein abundance relative to controls, with upregulated proteins enriched in IFN-1 signaling, pyroptosis, and blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption pathways. Complement system overactivation in severe encephalitis cases emerged as a candidate marker of disease severity and a potential therapeutic target, underscoring the value of CSF proteomics for identifying actionable molecular signatures. A multi-system transcriptomic study of Zika virus (ZIKV) integrates data from human brain organoids, monocyte-derived dendritic cells, and PBMCs from infected patients to map interferonstimulated gene (ISG) regulation across infection stages. IFN-β treatment potently activated ISGs including IRF7 and IFITM3 in brain organoids, while single-cell transcriptomics revealed cellular heterogeneity in ISG responses. Cross-system analysis identified 22 shared ISGs, and LASSO regression nominated 11 diagnostic biomarker candidates. Functional siRNA knockdown confirmed that IFI35, IFI44, and OAS3 restrict ZIKV replication, bridging transcriptomic discovery to validated antiviral mechanisms.A machine learning and mathematical modeling study of Ebola virus disease (EVD) resolves a longstanding controversy over the role of IFN-I in disease outcome. Analysis of patient data from the 2014-2016 West Africa epidemic reveals that IFN-I responses precede symptom onset in survivors, whereas non-survivors mount equivalent responses 3-4 days later. This delay causes IFN-I and IL-12 signals to overlap in non-survivors, disrupting the sequential cytokine cues required for effective T cell activation. The findings elevate temporal immune dynamics as a critical yet underappreciated determinant of host protection versus pathology.An integrated metabolomics-transcriptomics study of dengue virus (DENV) infection profiles plasma from 41 patients and 23 healthy controls using LC-MS and GC-MS, identifying 197 differentially abundant metabolites. Top upregulated species including trans-cinnamic acid and Lacetylcarnitine are proposed as diagnostic biomarkers by ROC analysis. KEGG and GSEA analyses highlighted disruption of ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporters as a key metabolic perturbation, corroborated by transcriptomic integration from GEO datasets identifying ABCC5, ABCB1, and ABCG5 as hub targets, opening a new avenue for understanding DENV-induced cellular pathology.A longitudinal study of 157 COVID-19 patients examines expression of TLR7, TYK2, and OAS1 across disease severity groups. Low TLR7 expression robustly correlates with severity and viremia, while OAS1 persists in severe cases with high viral loads even as TLR7 declines during recovery. The interdependence of these innate immune genes highlights the coordinated yet severity-stratified nature of early antiviral responses to SARS-CoV-2 and has implications for prognostic stratification.A study examines how transcription factors EB (TFEB) and E3 (TFE3), master regulators of lysosomal biogenesis, modulate viral replication, autophagy, and apoptosis across three coronavirus genera: gamma coronavirus IBV, beta coronavirus HCoV-OC43, and alpha coronavirus PEDV. Infection upregulates TFEB/TFE3 and induces a lysosomal stress response. TFE3 knockdown reveals its predominant role in controlling replication and cell death, with synergistic TFEB/TFE3 effects in IBV-and HCoV-OC43-infected cells. Brefeldin A experiments further establish that HCoV-OC43 egress occurs via the lysosomal pathway, identifying TFEB/TFE3-governed lysosomal biology as a conserved host vulnerability across coronavirus genera.A transcriptomic investigation of African swine fever virus (ASFV) addresses its strict tropism for primary porcine alveolar macrophages (PAMs) versus limited replication in immortalized macrophage lines (iPAMs). Comparative profiling of the SY-1 strain reveals divergent host responses: iPAMs predominantly engage lipid metabolism and oxidative stress, whereas PAMs activate cytokine signaling and broad immune effector programs. Reduced replication in iPAMs thus reflects a fundamentally different cellular environment, not merely receptor availability. Functional validation identifies JPH4 and CYP1A1 as candidate host permissiveness factors, providing a foundation for improved in vitro models and antiviral strategies-critical given the absence of licensed ASF vaccines.Together, these seven articles demonstrate the power of integrated multi-omics and systems approaches to decode host-virus interactions. Cross-cutting themes include the centrality and context-dependence of IFN-I signaling, the importance of temporal immune dynamics, the utility of multi-omics integration for biomarker discovery, and the value of appropriate cell and patient models for mechanistic investigation. We thank all contributing authors and reviewers, and hope this collection advances the development of novel diagnostics and host-targeted therapeutics for viral infectious diseases.Keywords: host-virus interactions, genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, interferon signaling, innate immunity, viral infectious diseases, systems biology, multi-omics

title_original: Editorial: Integrated genomic and systems approaches to unravel host-virus interactions in viral infectious diseases

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the need to decode host-virus interactions in viral infectious diseases through integrated multi-omics and systems approaches, aiming to advance the development of novel diagnostics and host-targeted therapeutics.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The editorial reviews seven primary research articles investigating host-virus interactions across various viral diseases, including VZV, ZIKV, Ebola, DENV, SARS-CoV-2, coronaviruses, and ASFV, using diverse models such as CSF, brain organoids, patient blood, and porcine macrophages.
analysis.methods: The included studies employed cross-system analysis, LASSO regression, functional siRNA knockdown, LC-MS and GC-MS metabolomics, single-cell transcriptomics, and mathematical modeling to identify biomarkers and validate antiviral mechanisms.
analysis.main_results: CSF proteomics in VZV CNS infection revealed elevated protein abundance in IFN-1 signaling and BBB disruption pathways, while ZIKV multi-system transcriptomics identified 22 shared ISGs and 11 diagnostic biomarker candidates, and Ebola virus disease modeling showed delayed IFN-I responses in non-survivors.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret these findings as demonstrating the power of integrated multi-omics to uncover context-dependent IFN-I signaling, temporal immune dynamics, and conserved host vulnerabilities, thereby advancing mechanistic investigation and therapeutic target identification.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings highlight the utility of multi-omics integration for biomarker discovery and the importance of appropriate cell and patient models, offering a foundation for improved in vitro models, antiviral strategies, and prognostic stratification.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate, as the editorial synthesizes findings from seven primary studies with varying designs and models, and the provided evidence does not explicitly assess generalizability or bias.

analysis.summary_en: This editorial synthesizes seven primary research articles that utilize integrated multi-omics and systems approaches to decode host-virus interactions across diverse viral infectious diseases. The studies investigate viruses targeting the central nervous system (VZV), Zika virus (ZIKV), Ebola virus disease (EVD), dengue virus (DENV), SARS-CoV-2, coronaviruses, and African swine fever virus (ASFV). Key findings include the identification of CSF proteomic signatures in VZV CNS infection, the discovery of interferon-stimulated gene (ISG) regulation and diagnostic biomarkers in ZIKV, and the elucidation of delayed IFN-I responses in Ebola non-survivors. The authors conclude that cross-cutting themes such as the centrality and context-dependence of IFN-I signaling, the importance of temporal immune dynamics, and the utility of multi-omics integration for biomarker discovery are critical for advancing the development of novel diagnostics and host-targeted therapeutics.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究解决了通过集成多组学和系统方法解码病毒传染病中 宿主 与病毒相互作用的需求,旨在推进新型诊断和 宿主 靶向治疗的开发。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该社论回顾了七篇主要研究文章,使用脑脊液、脑类器官、患者血液和猪巨噬细胞等不同模型,调查 宿主 病毒在各种病毒性疾病中的相互作用,包括 VZV、ZIKV、埃博拉、DENV、SARS-CoV-2、冠状病毒和 ASFV。
elements_zh.methods: 纳入的研究采用跨系统分析、LASSO 回归、功能性 siRNA 敲低、LC-MS 和 GC-MS 代谢组学、单细胞转录组学和数学模型来识别生物标志物并验证 抗病毒药物 机制。
elements_zh.main_results: VZV CNS 感染中的 CSF 蛋白质组学显示 IFN-1 信号传导和 BBB 破坏途径中的蛋白质丰度升高,而 ZIKV 多系统转录组学鉴定了 22 个共享 ISG 和 11 个候选诊断生物标志物,埃博拉病毒病 模型显示非幸存者中 IFN-I 反应延迟。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为证明了整合多组学的力量,可以揭示背景依赖性 IFN-I 信号传导、时间免疫动力学和保守的 宿主 漏洞,从而推进机制研究和治疗靶标识别。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现强调了多组学整合在生物标志物发现中的实用性以及适当的细胞和患者模型的重要性,为改进体外模型、抗病毒药物 策略和预后分层提供了基础。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据强度中等,因为社论综合了七项具有不同设计和模型的主要研究的结果,并且提供的证据没有明确评估普遍性或偏见。

abstract_zh: 两项贡献研究了针对中枢神经系统 (CNS) 的病毒。对 69 名水痘带状疱疹病毒 (VZV) 中枢神经系统感染患者的脑脊液 (CSF) 进行的临床和蛋白质组学分析记录了头痛、发烧和运动/感觉障碍的主要表现。CSF 蛋白质组学显示,相对于对照,CSF 蛋白质丰度显着升高,上调的蛋白质富含 IFN-1 信号传导、细胞焦亡和血脑屏障 (BBB) 破坏途径。严重脑炎病例中的补体系统过度激活成为疾病严重程度的候选标志物和潜在的治疗靶点,强调了脑脊液蛋白质组学在识别可操作分子特征方面的价值。寨卡病毒 (ZIKV) 的多系统转录组学研究整合了来自受感染患者的人脑类器官、单核细胞衍生的树突状细胞和 PBMC 的数据,以绘制跨感染阶段的干扰素刺激基因 (ISG) 调控图谱。IFN-β 治疗 有效激活脑类器官中的 ISG,包括 IRF7 和 IFITM3,而单细胞转录组学揭示了 ISG 反应的细胞异质性。跨系统分析确定了 22 个共享 ISG,LASSO 回归提名了 11 个候选诊断生物标志物。功能性 siRNA 敲低证实 IFI35、IFI44 和 OAS3 限制 ZIKV 复制,将转录组学发现与经过验证的 抗病毒药物 机制联系起来。埃博拉病毒病 (EVD) 的机器学习和数学模型研究解决了关于 IFN-I 在疾病结果中的作用的长期争议。对 2014-2016 年西非流行病患者数据的分析表明,幸存者中的 IFN-I 反应先于症状出现,而非幸存者则在 3-4 天后出现相同的反应。这种延迟导致 IFN-I 和 IL-12 信号在非幸存者中重叠,从而破坏了有效 T 细胞激活所需的连续细胞因子线索。这些发现将时间免疫动态提升为 宿主 保护与病理的关键但未被充分认识的决定因素。登革热病毒 (DENV) 感染的综合代谢组学-转录组学研究使用 LC-MS 和 GC-MS 对 41 名患者和 23 名健康对照者的血浆进行了分析,鉴定出 197 种差异丰富的代谢物。通过 ROC 分析,建议将上调最多的物种(包括反式肉桂酸和左旋乙酰肉碱)作为诊断生物标志物。KEGG 和 GSEA 分析强调 ATP 结合盒 (ABC) 转运蛋白的破坏是一个关键的代谢扰动,GEO 数据集的转录组整合将 ABCC5、ABCB1 和 ABCG5 识别为中心目标,证实了这一点,为理解 DENV 诱导的细胞病理学开辟了新途径。一项针对 157 名 COVID-19 患者的纵向研究检查了不同疾病严重程度组中 TLR7、TYK2 和 OAS1 的表达。TLR7 低表达与严重程度和病毒血症密切相关,而 OAS1 在病毒载量较高的重症病例中持续存在,即使 TLR7 在恢复过程中下降。这些先天免疫基因的相互依赖性凸显了早期 抗病毒药物 对 SARS-CoV-2 反应的协调性和严重性分层性质,并对预后分层具有影响。一项研究探讨了转录因子 EB (TFEB) 和 E3 (TFE3)(溶酶体生物发生的主要调节因子)如何调节三个冠状病毒属的病毒复制、自噬和细胞凋亡:γ 冠状病毒 IBV、β 冠状病毒 HCoV-OC43 和甲型冠状病毒 PEDV。感染上调 TFEB/TFE3 并诱导溶酶体应激反应。TFE3 敲低揭示了其在控制复制和细胞死亡中的主要作用,在 IBV 和 HCoV-OC43 感染的细胞中具有协同 TFEB/TFE3 效应。Brefeldin A 实验进一步证实 HCoV-OC43 的流出是通过溶酶体途径发生的,将 TFEB/TFE3 控制的溶酶体生物学确定为跨冠状病毒属的保守 宿主 脆弱性。非洲猪瘟病毒 (ASFV) 的转录组学研究解决了其对原代猪肺泡巨噬细胞 (PAM) 的严格趋向性与在永生化巨噬细胞系中有限复制的问题(iPAM)。SY-1 菌株的比较分析揭示了不同的 宿主 反应:iPAM 主要参与脂质代谢和氧化应激,而 PAM 则激活细胞因子信号传导和广泛的免疫效应程序。因此,iPAM 中复制的减少反映了根本不同的细胞环境,而不仅仅是受体的可用性。功能验证将 JPH4 和 CYP1A1 确定为候选 宿主 许可因子,为改进体外模型和 抗病毒药物 策略奠定了基础,鉴于缺乏获得许可的 ASF 疫苗,这至关重要。这七篇文章共同证明了集成多组学和系统方法解码 宿主-病毒相互作用的强大功能。交叉主题包括 IFN-I 信号传导的中心性和背景依赖性、时间免疫动力学的重要性、多组学整合在生物标志物发现中的实用性,以及适当的细胞和患者模型对机制研究的价值。我们感谢所有贡献的作者和审稿人,并希望该合集能够促进病毒传染病的新型诊断和 宿主 靶向治疗的发展。关键词:宿主-病毒相互作用、基因组学、转录组学、蛋白质组学、代谢组学、干扰素信号传导、先天免疫、病毒传染病、系统生物学、多组学

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究解决了通过集成多组学和系统方法解码病毒传染病中 宿主 与病毒相互作用的需求,旨在推进新型诊断和 宿主 靶向治疗的开发。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该社论回顾了七篇主要研究文章,使用脑脊液、脑类器官、患者血液和猪巨噬细胞等不同模型,调查 宿主 病毒在各种病毒性疾病中的相互作用,包括 VZV、ZIKV、埃博拉、DENV、SARS-CoV-2、冠状病毒和 ASFV。
analysis_zh.methods: 纳入的研究采用跨系统分析、LASSO 回归、功能性 siRNA 敲低、LC-MS 和 GC-MS 代谢组学、单细胞转录组学和数学模型来识别生物标志物并验证 抗病毒药物 机制。
analysis_zh.main_results: VZV CNS 感染中的 CSF 蛋白质组学显示 IFN-1 信号传导和 BBB 破坏途径中的蛋白质丰度升高,而 ZIKV 多系统转录组学鉴定了 22 个共享 ISG 和 11 个候选诊断生物标志物,埃博拉病毒病 模型显示非幸存者中 IFN-I 反应延迟。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为证明了整合多组学的力量,可以揭示背景依赖性 IFN-I 信号传导、时间免疫动力学和保守的 宿主 漏洞,从而推进机制研究和治疗靶标识别。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现强调了多组学整合在生物标志物发现中的实用性以及适当的细胞和患者模型的重要性,为改进体外模型、抗病毒药物 策略和预后分层提供了基础。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据强度中等,因为社论综合了七项具有不同设计和模型的主要研究的结果,并且提供的证据没有明确评估普遍性或偏见。

title: It’s not just virology: The Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda demands a wider public health response
abstract: The current outbreak of Ebola disease caused by the Bundibugyo virus (species Orthoebolavirus bundibugyoense) in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda is much more than another infectious disease emergency. It reminds us that epidemics come not only from biological pathogens but also from social inequities, environmental disruption, fragile health systems, and persistent armed conflict. While Ebola captures headlines because of its fear-provoking symptoms and high mortality, the conditions that allow it to spread receive far less attention.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是对刚果民主共和国和乌干达当前埃博拉病毒 暴发 的评论,重点关注本迪布焦病毒。
elements_zh.methods: 作者通过检查允许病毒传播的条件(例如引起恐惧的症状和高 暴发)以及导致其持续存在的社会决定因素来分析 暴发。
elements_zh.main_results: 作者观察到,虽然埃博拉病毒因其令人恐惧的症状和高 死亡率 而成为头条新闻,但促进其传播的潜在条件却很少受到关注。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究将 暴发 解释为一场多方面的危机,需要采取更广泛的公共卫生应对措施,不仅限于病毒学,还要解决社会和系统因素。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,有效控制埃博拉病毒需要在医疗干预措施的同时解决社会不平等、环境破坏和脆弱的卫生系统问题。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是评论性的,缺乏实证数据,限制了其提供定量证据的能力;由于其描述性,证据强度较低。

title_zh: 这不仅仅是病毒学:刚果民主共和国和乌干达的本迪布焦埃博拉病毒 暴发 需要更广泛的公共卫生应对措施
source_body_en: The current outbreak of Ebola disease caused by the Bundibugyo virus (species Orthoebolavirus bundibugyoense) in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda is much more than another infectious disease emergency. It reminds us that epidemics come not only from biological pathogens but also from social inequities, environmental disruption, fragile health systems, and persistent armed conflict. While Ebola captures headlines because of its fear-provoking symptoms and high mortality, the conditions that allow it to spread receive far less attention.
abstract_zh: 当前刚果民主共和国(DRC)和乌干达由本迪布焦病毒(本迪布焦正埃博拉病毒属)引起的埃博拉疫情不仅仅是另一种传染病紧急情况。它提醒我们,流行病不仅来自生物病原体,还来自社会不平等、环境破坏、脆弱的卫生系统和持续的武装冲突。虽然埃博拉病毒因其令人恐惧的症状和高 死亡率 而成为头条新闻,但导致其传播的条件却很少受到关注。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究提出了对刚果民主共和国和乌干达的本迪布焦埃博拉病毒 暴发 采取更广泛的公共卫生应对措施的必要性,强调流行病源于生物病原体以及社会不平等、环境破坏、脆弱的卫生系统和持续的武装冲突。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是对刚果民主共和国和乌干达当前埃博拉病毒 暴发 的评论,重点关注本迪布焦病毒。
analysis_zh.methods: 作者通过检查允许病毒传播的条件(例如引起恐惧的症状和高 暴发)以及导致其持续存在的社会决定因素来分析 暴发。
analysis_zh.main_results: 作者观察到,虽然埃博拉病毒因其令人恐惧的症状和高 死亡率 而成为头条新闻,但促进其传播的潜在条件却很少受到关注。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究将 暴发 解释为一场多方面的危机,需要采取更广泛的公共卫生应对措施,不仅限于病毒学,还要解决社会和系统因素。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,有效控制埃博拉病毒需要在医疗干预措施的同时解决社会不平等、环境破坏和脆弱的卫生系统问题。

title: Más Allá del Ébola: Cultura Preventiva y Vigilancia Epidemiológica Ante el Mundial Fifa 2026. La Vigilancia Epidemiológica Protege a la Población; la Educación Construye una Sociedad Capaz de Protegerse a Sí Misma
abstract: The Ebola virus disease has represented one of the greatest challenges to global public health, not only because of its high mortality rate, but also because it highlighted the limitations of healthcare systems and the importance of societal preparedness for emerging diseases. Drawing on the lessons learned from the West African epidemic (2014–2016), this essay reflects on health preparedness in the context of the 2026 FIFA World Cup, emphasizing that epidemiological surveillance, diagnostic capacity, and institutional coordination are indispensable pillars, but insufficient without an informed population committed to prevention. Through the analysis of documents from international organizations and recent experience in preparing for mass events, this essay argues that health education, risk communication, and the development of a preventive culture are essential elements for strengthening the resilience of societies to future health emergencies. It is concluded that the greatest legacy of Ebola transcends the scientific and technological advances achieved in recent decades, demonstrating that prevention must be understood as an ongoing educational process capable of transforming knowledge into responsible behavior. In this sense, building a culture of prevention from childhood is a fundamental strategy for protecting public health and strengthening preparedness for future epidemiological challenges.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the persistent public-health threat posed by Ebola virus disease and the need to translate lessons from the 2014–2016 West African epidemic into preparedness for future mass gatherings such as the 2026 FIFA World Cup.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The authors present a reflective essay that synthesizes international guidance and recent experience in preparing for mass events, focusing on the role of epidemiological surveillance, diagnostic capacity, institutional coordination, and societal education.
analysis.methods: The work is based on document analysis of international organizational reports and experiential evidence from mass-event preparedness, integrating qualitative synthesis rather than primary data collection or laboratory assays.
analysis.main_results: The essay concludes that prevention must be framed as an ongoing educational process that transforms knowledge into responsible behavior, with childhood education identified as a key strategy for building a culture of prevention.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the Ebola epidemic’s legacy as demonstrating that scientific advances alone are insufficient without societal preparedness, emphasizing the novelty of positioning education and preventive culture as central pillars of resilience.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings imply that integrating risk communication and preventive education into public-health planning can enhance societal resilience to future health emergencies, particularly in the context of large-scale events.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence base is limited to a qualitative synthesis of documents and experiences, lacking primary data, quantitative outcomes, or causal inference, which constrains the strength of the conclusions to low.

analysis.summary_en: This reflective essay examines how lessons from the 2014–2016 Ebola epidemic can inform preparedness for the 2026 FIFA World Cup, arguing that epidemiological surveillance and institutional coordination must be paired with societal education and a preventive culture. The authors synthesize international guidance and recent mass-event preparedness experiences to conclude that prevention is an ongoing educational process requiring childhood education to build resilient societies. They emphasize that the greatest legacy of Ebola is not merely scientific advances but the transformation of knowledge into responsible behavior. The work highlights the need to integrate risk communication and preventive education into public-health planning for future health emergencies.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究解决了 埃博拉病毒病 造成的持续公共卫生威胁,以及将 2014-2016 年西非疫情的经验教训转化为为未来大型集会(如 2026 年 FIFA 世界杯)做好准备的必要性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 作者提出了一篇反思性文章,综合了准备群众活动的国际指导和最新经验,重点关注流行病学 监测 的作用、诊断能力、机构协调和社会教育。
elements_zh.methods: 这项工作基于国际组织报告的文件分析和群体事件准备的经验证据,整合了定性综合而不是原始数据收集或实验室分析。
elements_zh.main_results: 本文的结论是,预防必须被视为一个持续的教育过程,将知识转化为负责任的行为,并将儿童教育确定为建立预防文化的关键策略。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将埃博拉疫情的遗产解释为,如果没有社会准备,仅靠科学进步是不够的,并强调将教育和预防文化作为复原力的核心支柱的新颖性。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the persistent public-health threat posed by Ebola virus disease and the need to translate lessons from the 2014–2016 West African epidemic into preparedness for future mass gatherings such as the 2026 FIFA World Cup.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The authors present a reflective essay that synthesizes international guidance and recent experience in preparing for mass events, focusing on the role of epidemiological surveillance, diagnostic capacity, institutional coordination, and societal education.
analysis_en.methods: The work is based on document analysis of international organizational reports and experiential evidence from mass-event preparedness, integrating qualitative synthesis rather than primary data collection or laboratory assays.
analysis_en.main_results: The essay concludes that prevention must be framed as an ongoing educational process that transforms knowledge into responsible behavior, with childhood education identified as a key strategy for building a culture of prevention.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the Ebola epidemic’s legacy as demonstrating that scientific advances alone are insufficient without societal preparedness, emphasizing the novelty of positioning education and preventive culture as central pillars of resilience.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings imply that integrating risk communication and preventive education into public-health planning can enhance societal resilience to future health emergencies, particularly in the context of large-scale events.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence base is limited to a qualitative synthesis of documents and experiences, lacking primary data, quantitative outcomes, or causal inference, which constrains the strength of the conclusions to low.

title_zh: Más Allá del Ébola: Cultura Preventiva y Vigilancia Epidemiológica Ante el Mundial Fifa 2026. La Vigilancia Epidemiológica Protege a la Población;米斯玛保护社会教育建设
source_body_en: The Ebola virus disease has represented one of the greatest challenges to global public health, not only because of its high mortality rate, but also because it highlighted the limitations of healthcare systems and the importance of societal preparedness for emerging diseases. Drawing on the lessons learned from the West African epidemic (2014–2016), this essay reflects on health preparedness in the context of the 2026 FIFA World Cup, emphasizing that epidemiological surveillance, diagnostic capacity, and institutional coordination are indispensable pillars, but insufficient without an informed population committed to prevention. Through the analysis of documents from international organizations and recent experience in preparing for mass events, this essay argues that health education, risk communication, and the development of a preventive culture are essential elements for strengthening the resilience of societies to future health emergencies. It is concluded that the greatest legacy of Ebola transcends the scientific and technological advances achieved in recent decades, demonstrating that prevention must be understood as an ongoing educational process capable of transforming knowledge into responsible behavior. In this sense, building a culture of prevention from childhood is a fundamental strategy for protecting public health and strengthening preparedness for future epidemiological challenges.
abstract_zh: 埃博拉病毒病 代表了全球公共卫生面临的最大挑战之一,不仅因为其高 死亡率 比率,还因为它强调了医疗保健系统的局限性以及社会对新出现疾病做好准备的重要性。本文借鉴西非疫情(2014-2016)的经验教训,反思了 2026 年 FIFA 世界杯背景下的卫生准备工作,强调流行病学 监测、诊断能力和机构协调是不可或缺的支柱,但如果没有知情民众致力于预防,这些支柱就不够。通过对国际组织的文件和近期准备群众活动的经验的分析,本文认为健康教育、风险沟通和预防文化的发展是增强社会应对未来突发卫生事件的抵御能力的基本要素。结论是,埃博拉病毒最伟大的遗产超越了近几十年来所取得的科学和技术进步,这表明预防必须被理解为一个持续的教育过程,能够将知识转化为负责任的行为。从这个意义上说,从儿童时期构建预防文化是保护公众健康、加强应对未来流行病学挑战的基本战略。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究解决了 埃博拉病毒病 造成的持续公共卫生威胁,以及将 2014-2016 年西非疫情的经验教训转化为为未来大型集会(如 2026 年 FIFA 世界杯)做好准备的必要性。

title: Screening and monitoring of travellers returning from countries affected by Bundibugyo virus: an overview of European approaches, July 2026
abstract: The 2026 Ebola outbreak caused by Bundibugyo virus in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda has prompted European countries and the United States to revise measures for travellers, healthcare workers and humanitarian personnel returning from affected areas. We compare current procedures and protocols with those implemented during the 2013-2016 Ebola outbreak. Despite some national differences, policies have largely converged towards risk-based management, early case detection, rapid isolation, exposure-based monitoring and healthcare preparedness, rather than routine border screening.
authors: on behalf of the European HLIU Network

elements_zh.methods: 该研究涉及对国家政策和协议的比较分析,研究方法随时间的变化和趋同。

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果为欧洲公共卫生战略提供了管理从本迪布焦病毒影响地区返回的旅行者的信息,强调做好准备和有针对性的监测而不是边境筛查。

title: Exploring the Potential Contribution of Climate-Informed Research to Future Ebola Preparedness in Central Africa
abstract: The ongoing 2026 Bundibugyo ebolavirus outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo highlights the continued vulnerability of Central Africa to recurrent Ebola emergence. This outbreak emerged less than six months after the previous one ended, appears to represent one of the shortest documented inter-epidemic intervals in the Democratic Republic of the Congo based on currently available outbreak reports. Current surveillance systems remain largely reactive, focusing on the detection of human cases after zoonotic spillover has occurred. While strengthening health systems, diagnostic capacity, and early case detection remains the cornerstone of Ebola preparedness, growing research suggests that environmental and climatic information may eventually contribute to a broader understanding of spillover risk within a One Health framework. However, current evidence remains insufficient to identify validated environmental indicators or operational thresholds capable of predicting Ebola spillover events. Recent modeling studies have demonstrated that environmental drivers of Ebola emergence remain highly context-dependent and cannot yet support operational early warning systems. This commentary argues that continued research integrating environmental monitoring, remote sensing, ecological observations, and epidemiological data may improve understanding of Ebola emergence and eventually contribute to future preparedness strategies. Rather than proposing climate-informed preparedness approaches as an operational prediction tool, we emphasize its potential as a complementary research priority requiring further validation before any operational implementation.

Current surveillance systems remain largely reactive, focusing on the detection of human cases after zoonotic spillover has occurred. While strengthening health systems, diagnostic capacity, and early case detection remains the cornerstone of Ebola preparedness, growing research suggests that environmental and climatic information may eventually contribute to a broader understanding of spillover risk within a One Health framework. However, current evidence remains insufficient to identify validated environmental indicators or operational thresholds capable of predicting Ebola spillover events. Recent modeling studies have demonstrated that environmental drivers of Ebola emergence remain highly context-dependent and cannot yet support operational early warning systems. This commentary argues that continued research integrating environmental monitoring, remote sensing, ecological observations, and epidemiological data may improve understanding of Ebola emergence and eventually contribute to future preparedness strategies. Rather than proposing climate-informed preparedness approaches as an operational prediction tool, we emphasize its potential as a complementary research priority requiring further validation before any operational implementation.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 刚果民主共和国东部持续存在的 2026 年本迪布焦埃博拉病毒 暴发 凸显了中部非洲对于埃博拉反复出现的持续脆弱性。这项研究探讨了气候信息研究对该地区未来埃博拉病毒防范的潜在贡献。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是一篇评论文章,回顾了当前的 监测 系统以及与中部非洲埃博拉疫情相关的环境和气候信息研究。
elements_zh.methods: 该评论整合了最近的模型研究结果,并强调需要继续结合环境监测、遥感、生态观测和流行病学数据进行研究。
elements_zh.main_results: 最近的建模研究表明,埃博拉病毒出现的环境驱动因素仍然高度依赖于具体情况,尚不能支持预警系统的运行。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 评论认为,基于气候的研究可以增进对埃博拉病毒出现的了解,并有助于未来的防备策略,但目前的证据不足以进行操作预测。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调了气候知情研究在加强埃博拉防备方面的潜力,强调在实施之前需要进一步验证。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据仍然不足以确定能够预测埃博拉 跨物种溢出 事件的有效环境指标或操作阈值,这表明需要进一步研究。

abstract_zh: 刚果民主共和国东部持续存在的 2026 年本迪布焦埃博拉病毒 暴发 凸显了中部非洲对于埃博拉反复出现的持续脆弱性。这次 暴发 出现在上一次 暴发 结束后不到六个月的时间里,根据目前可用的 暴发 报告,这似乎是刚果民主共和国有记录的最短的流行病间隔之一。目前的 监测 系统在很大程度上仍处于反应状态,重点是在人畜共患病 跨物种溢出 发生后检测人类病例。虽然加强卫生系统、诊断能力和早期病例检测仍然是埃博拉病毒防范的基石,但越来越多的研究表明,环境和气候信息最终可能有助于在“同一个健康”框架内更广泛地了解 跨物种溢出 风险。然而,目前的证据仍然不足以确定能够预测埃博拉 跨物种溢出 事件的经过验证的环境指标或操作阈值。最近的建模研究表明,埃博拉病毒出现的环境驱动因素仍然高度依赖于具体情况,尚不能支持预警系统的运行。该评论认为,整合环境监测、遥感、生态观察和流行病学数据的持续研究可能会增进对埃博拉疫情的了解,并最终有助于未来的防备策略。我们没有提出将气候知情的准备方法作为一种业务预测工具,而是强调其作为补充研究优先事项的潜力,需要在任何业务实施之前进行进一步验证。

title: Design of Epitope-Focused Vaccines via Epitope Cleavage
abstract: High Resolution Image Download MS PowerPoint Slide The design of epitope-focused immunogens that steer serum antibody responses toward epitopes targeted by broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) is a promising approach to develop broad-spectrum vaccines against pathogens with high genetic variability. Here, we introduce a strategy called epitope cleavage, which involves “cleaving” an epitope to steer antibodies away from it onto other regions of an antigen. We demonstrated the utility of epitope cleavage using two independent approaches: circular permutation and proteolytic cleavage. We first designed a sarbecovirus vaccine candidate by circularly permuting the receptor binding domain (RBD) of the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) spike protein; we next designed broad Ebolavirus immunogens by inserting the TEV protease cleavage site into the glycan cap of Ebola glycoprotein (GP) for site-specific epitope cleavage. By cleaving variable regions on each antigen, both the circular permuted RBD and cleaved GPs elicited antibodies with enhanced cross-reactivity to related viruses compared to unmodified antigen and exhibited a reduction in antibody responses toward the “cleaved” epitope. Our results present epitope cleavage as a vaccine design strategy that redirects antibody responses without compromising immunogenicity.

The researchers demonstrated this approach using two methods: circular permutation of the receptor binding domain (RBD) of the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein and proteolytic cleavage of the glycan cap of Ebola glycoprotein (GP). full_text: The Democratic Republic of the Congo has declared its seventeenth Ebola outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo virus, which had been circulating undetected for months. The response is now catching up across a region weakened by conflict, displacement and loss of humanitarian aid. With no licensed vaccine or treatment, containment will depend on rebuilding resources, access and trust in public health systems. The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and its neighbouring countries face an incredible challenge in the new Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) disease outbreak. By the time the Institut National de Recherche Biomédicale in Kinshasa confirmed BDBV in Ituri Province, officials had already recorded 246 suspected cases and 80 suspected deaths across several health zones. Confirmed cases were soon logged across multiple DRC provinces and in Kampala, the capital of neighbouring Uganda1. The WHO declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern on 17 May, and the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention followed with a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security on 18 May, naming ten other countries at high risk of spread2,3. The scale of those initial figures made it evident that the world was not discovering a new outbreak so much as uncovering one that had been silently circulating, hidden by the fragility of local healthcare capacity and propagated by conflict, community distrust and population mobility. As of 31 May, 336 cases had been confirmed across both countries, with 49 confirmed deaths, alongside 220 suspected cases and 236 suspected deaths in the DRC. These numbers are almost certainly an undercount. A modelling group at Imperial College London estimated within days of the declaration that true infections probably already exceeded 900, and many community deaths have never entered a formal record4. Unlike West Africa in 2013, where the index case seeded a region with no prior filovirus experience, the DRC and its neighbours have extensive experience with viral haemorrhagic fevers, including 10 outbreaks in the past 5 years alone. The communities and health workers of the region have shown remarkable resilience across these repeated emergencies, carrying the burden of response, often at great personal cost, with limited and intermittent external support. However, a confluence of factors is lining up to make this outbreak at least the second-biggest Ebola crisis the world has seen. First, delayed laboratory identification allowed geographic expansion, and the response is now playing catch-up. The initial delay followed negative Ebola testing at the provincial laboratory in Bunia, which required specimens to be sent to Kinshasa for species-specific confirmation. Even before the 5 May alert to the WHO, some unexplained illnesses had been noted in the region with negative testing for common pathogens, highlighting regional blind spots leading to the current crisis, which may have resulted from sudden withdrawal of aid. The United States Agency for International Development (USAID) was historically the DRC’s largest humanitarian donor and since its dissolution the DRC has seen surge in cholera, mpox and measles across its eastern provinces, conditions under which an uncommon disease is far harder to distinguish from the common ones5. Although most cases remain in Ituri, patients have been confirmed hundreds of kilometres away in North and South Kivu Provinces, in eastern DRC. These multiple fronts require already-strained resources — treatment units, infection prevention and sanitation supplies, contact tracers, laboratory capacity and community engagement — to be divided even further. Financial commitments have been made by the national government and the global community, but there is typically a lag between the appropriation of funds and their conversion into contracts, procurement and distribution, making this the most precarious moment of the response. Reports from affected areas indicate that personal protective equipment and diagnostic supplies are severely lagging behind need6. Active conflict is impeding access, and that conflict has worsened with the withdrawal of aid that followed the dismantling of USAID. On 28 May, the WHO Director-General travelled to the DRC to appeal for a ceasefire, enabling central outbreak control efforts to continue: bringing sick patients into isolation, assuring them they will be safe as they receive care, and tracing their contacts across an insecure terrain. In this outbreak, trust is as valuable and critical as monetary funds. A population-based survey during the 2018–2019 North Kivu outbreak found that only about a third of respondents trusted that local authorities represented their interests, and a quarter believed the outbreak was not real7. During that outbreak, the WHO recorded roughly 390 attacks on health facilities and workers in 2019 (ref. 8). The same dynamics are now compounded by displacement and the loss of the previously funded community programmes. Because there have been only two previous outbreaks, research on BDBV medical countermeasures lags between that for Zaire and Sudan ebolaviruses, for which there are either approved products or more products with safety and efficacy data. Although arrangements for vaccine and therapeutic trials are underway, the manufacturing and trial timelines mean deployment is likely to be months away9. Their capacity to alter the trajectory of this outbreak, at least in the near term, is therefore limited. And that trajectory is concerning. The outbreak will probably continue for months, potentially into 2027, with a high risk of spread into areas hosting displaced and refugee populations and across borders, making regional collaboration essential. Although BDBV is unlikely to cause a pandemic, as cases rise, sporadic suspect cases may surface in travellers worldwide, particularly given the nonspecific early symptoms of Ebola. Despite the alarm these cases generate, the base rate of true infection among travellers is very low, and the overwhelming majority of suspected cases evaluated elsewhere will test negative. BDBV mortality has ranged from 30% to 50% in the historical record, lower than the roughly 40–66% seen in large Zaire ebolavirus outbreaks. But those estimates rest on a small number of patients, and case fatality rates shift over the arc of an outbreak. Early mortality may be high, reflecting delays in reaching care and a shortage of treatment resources. As more resources arrive, a falling case fatality rate would indicate two improvements at once: better success in building trust and bringing patients in, and better supportive care once they arrive. The current numbers could be read as a measure of the response’s reach as well as the virus’s lethality. Lastly, the current outbreak is occurring in the middle of another underlying shift: US global aid architecture is shifting towards new approaches, such as ‘America First’ bilateral agreements, rather than investment in multilateral and sector-wide health programmes. African countries are re-examining how regional commitments can be consolidated to build a safer, more self-reliant future10. The containment of Bundibugyo virus outbreak, and the inevitable outbreaks that will follow it, will require consistent commitment on both fronts at once: regional investment that builds standing capacity where these viruses emerge, and global solidarity that is durable rather than episodic. A reactive posture, in which funding is surged only after a crisis has occurred, leaves us backfooted, particularly in areas of complex humanitarian emergencies. This creates massive gaps in timely resources, the cost of which is paid in patient lives and healthcare worker safety. References - World Health Organization. full_text_sections.full_text: The Democratic Republic of the Congo has declared its seventeenth Ebola outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo virus, which had been circulating undetected for months. The response is now catching up across a region weakened by conflict, displacement and loss of humanitarian aid. With no licensed vaccine or treatment, containment will depend on rebuilding resources, access and trust in public health systems. The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and its neighbouring countries face an incredible challenge in the new Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) disease outbreak. By the time the Institut National de Recherche Biomédicale in Kinshasa confirmed BDBV in Ituri Province, officials had already recorded 246 suspected cases and 80 suspected deaths across several health zones. Confirmed cases were soon logged across multiple DRC provinces and in Kampala, the capital of neighbouring Uganda1. The WHO declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern on 17 May, and the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention followed with a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security on 18 May, naming ten other countries at high risk of spread2,3. The scale of those initial figures made it evident that the world was not discovering a new outbreak so much as uncovering one that had been silently circulating, hidden by the fragility of local healthcare capacity and propagated by conflict, community distrust and population mobility. As of 31 May, 336 cases had been confirmed across both countries, with 49 confirmed deaths, alongside 220 suspected cases and 236 suspected deaths in the DRC. These numbers are almost certainly an undercount. A modelling group at Imperial College London estimated within days of the declaration that true infections probably already exceeded 900, and many community deaths have never entered a formal record4. Unlike West Africa in 2013, where the index case seeded a region with no prior filovirus experience, the DRC and its neighbours have extensive experience with viral haemorrhagic fevers, including 10 outbreaks in the past 5 years alone. The communities and health workers of the region have shown remarkable resilience across these repeated emergencies, carrying the burden of response, often at great personal cost, with limited and intermittent external support. However, a confluence of factors is lining up to make this outbreak at least the second-biggest Ebola crisis the world has seen. First, delayed laboratory identification allowed geographic expansion, and the response is now playing catch-up. The initial delay followed negative Ebola testing at the provincial laboratory in Bunia, which required specimens to be sent to Kinshasa for species-specific confirmation. Even before the 5 May alert to the WHO, some unexplained illnesses had been noted in the region with negative testing for common pathogens, highlighting regional blind spots leading to the current crisis, which may have resulted from sudden withdrawal of aid. The United States Agency for International Development (USAID) was historically the DRC’s largest humanitarian donor and since its dissolution the DRC has seen surge in cholera, mpox and measles across its eastern provinces, conditions under which an uncommon disease is far harder to distinguish from the common ones5. Although most cases remain in Ituri, patients have been confirmed hundreds of kilometres away in North and South Kivu Provinces, in eastern DRC. These multiple fronts require already-strained resources — treatment units, infection prevention and sanitation supplies, contact tracers, laboratory capacity and community engagement — to be divided even further. Financial commitments have been made by the national government and the global community, but there is typically a lag between the appropriation of funds and their conversion into contracts, procurement and distribution, making this the most precarious moment of the response. Reports from affected areas indicate that personal protective equipment and diagnostic supplies are severely lagging behind need6. Active conflict is impeding access, and that conflict has worsened with the withdrawal of aid that followed the dismantling of USAID. On 28 May, the WHO Director-General travelled to the DRC to appeal for a ceasefire, enabling central outbreak control efforts to continue: bringing sick patients into isolation, assuring them they will be safe as they receive care, and tracing their contacts across an insecure terrain. In this outbreak, trust is as valuable and critical as monetary funds. A population-based survey during the 2018–2019 North Kivu outbreak found that only about a third of respondents trusted that local authorities represented their interests, and a quarter believed the outbreak was not real7. During that outbreak, the WHO recorded roughly 390 attacks on health facilities and workers in 2019 (ref. 8). The same dynamics are now compounded by displacement and the loss of the previously funded community programmes. Because there have been only two previous outbreaks, research on BDBV medical countermeasures lags between that for Zaire and Sudan ebolaviruses, for which there are either approved products or more products with safety and efficacy data. Although arrangements for vaccine and therapeutic trials are underway, the manufacturing and trial timelines mean deployment is likely to be months away9. Their capacity to alter the trajectory of this outbreak, at least in the near term, is therefore limited. And that trajectory is concerning. The outbreak will probably continue for months, potentially into 2027, with a high risk of spread into areas hosting displaced and refugee populations and across borders, making regional collaboration essential. Although BDBV is unlikely to cause a pandemic, as cases rise, sporadic suspect cases may surface in travellers worldwide, particularly given the nonspecific early symptoms of Ebola. Despite the alarm these cases generate, the base rate of true infection among travellers is very low, and the overwhelming majority of suspected cases evaluated elsewhere will test negative. BDBV mortality has ranged from 30% to 50% in the historical record, lower than the roughly 40–66% seen in large Zaire ebolavirus outbreaks. But those estimates rest on a small number of patients, and case fatality rates shift over the arc of an outbreak. Early mortality may be high, reflecting delays in reaching care and a shortage of treatment resources. As more resources arrive, a falling case fatality rate would indicate two improvements at once: better success in building trust and bringing patients in, and better supportive care once they arrive. The current numbers could be read as a measure of the response’s reach as well as the virus’s lethality. Lastly, the current outbreak is occurring in the middle of another underlying shift: US global aid architecture is shifting towards new approaches, such as ‘America First’ bilateral agreements, rather than investment in multilateral and sector-wide health programmes. African countries are re-examining how regional commitments can be consolidated to build a safer, more self-reliant future10. The containment of Bundibugyo virus outbreak, and the inevitable outbreaks that will follow it, will require consistent commitment on both fronts at once: regional investment that builds standing capacity where these viruses emerge, and global solidarity that is durable rather than episodic. A reactive posture, in which funding is surged only after a crisis has occurred, leaves us backfooted, particularly in areas of complex humanitarian emergencies. This creates massive gaps in timely resources, the cost of which is paid in patient lives and healthcare worker safety. References - World Health Organization. full_text: How a legacy of mistrust in DRC has led to 17 Ebola outbreaks in 50 years BMJ 2026; 394 doi: https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj-2026-100331 (Published 21 July 2026) Cite this as: BMJ 2026;394:e100331Seventeen Ebola outbreaks in 50 years. The same country, over and over again. On 17 May, the World Health Organization declared a public health emergency of international concern as Bundibugyo virus disease re-emerged in Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), spreading to Uganda within days.1 As of 8 July, 1759 suspected cases and 600 deaths had been reported across the provinces of Ituri and Nord-Kivu.2 The previous Ebola outbreak in DRC ended just five months previously. The one before that ended in 2021. The question is not why this outbreak occurred, but why DRC faces Ebola again and again, and what will finally break that cycle. The answer matters well beyond DRC’s borders. As outbreaks recur in the same fragile settings, global health institutions continue funding emergency response at the expense of the trust-building investments that might finally end the cycle. The answer lies in a convergence of structural vulnerabilities. DRC borders nine countries, and cross-border movement allows pathogens to outpace chronically underfunded local surveillance systems. Decades of armed conflict have displaced millions in the affected areas, leaving health facilities damaged and surveillance unable to distinguish Ebola from endemic febrile illness.3 Deforestation and agricultural expansion bring human populations into direct contact with the fruit bat species identified as the principal reservoir hosts for Ebola virus. Hunting and handling of bats as a protein source has been directly implicated in spillover events.45 Beneath these structural conditions lies a deeper vulnerability that epidemiological models consistently underestimate—the erosion of community trust in outside medical responders. Four days after WHO sounded the alarm, residents in Rwampara, Ituri, stormed an Ebola treatment facility and set it alight when authorities refused to release the body of a man who had died there. A day later, a tent at a Médecins Sans Frontières facility in nearby Mongbwalu was also burned.6 These were not isolated acts, nor were they justified. They were warning signs: the latest expression of a pattern throughout DRC’s long history of the disease in which communities, having learned to regard outside health responses with suspicion, signalled the collapse of legitimacy through the most visible means available to them. During the 2018 to 2020 outbreak, WHO documented approximately 390 attacks on health facilities: 11 health workers were killed and 83 were injured.7 A single phrase captured the sentiment across affected communities: “Ebola is a business.”8 This mistrust is not irrational, nor is it misinformation to be corrected with better messaging, though explaining its roots is not the same as excusing violence against health workers. It is a structured disposition rooted in history: colonial medicine that subjected central African populations to forced biomedical campaigns, a legacy that measurably reduces vaccination uptake and trust in medicine today;9 decades of state violence and institutional failure; and more recent Ebola responses that deployed security forces, imposed burial restrictions that disrupted community norms, and excluded local communities from recruitment as health workers and responders in ways that deepened the atmosphere of mistrust.8 When responders later announced experimental vaccines, communities whose trust had already been forfeited were alienated rather than reassured.8 Surveys confirmed that low institutional trust was among the strongest independent predictors of vaccine refusal and delayed care seeking.10 The distinction between community engagement and community ownership matters here. Engagement means communicating strategies designed by international organisations and central government agencies. Ownership means communities participating from the outset: controlling the pace of interventions, deciding on burial practices that respect both necessity and dignity, and having historical grievances treated as legitimate. This is harder and slower than deploying a response team with megaphones, but it is the approach most consistently associated with improved acceptance of public health measures and more effective outbreak control.78 Although vaccines, surveillance, and clinical care were indispensable, sustained community dialogue and increasing reliance on trusted local actors were equally critical to achieving control of the 2018 to 2020 outbreak. Breaking DRC’s cycle of Ebola outbreaks requires investment at two levels. In the current outbreak, these failures are already visible: burial teams have been attacked, patients have fled treatment centres, and frontline responders report that community members question whether the disease is real.11 In the short term, community trust must be treated not as a communication problem but as an operational prerequisite. Local health workers, traditional leaders, and religious figures must lead engagement rather than deliver externally designed messages; burial protocols must be negotiated, not imposed; and feedback mechanisms must let response strategy adapt in real time.7 Longer term, DRC and partners must invest in infrastructure that earns trust before the next outbreak, including functional health facilities, community rooted health workers, and water and sanitation foundations.34 Seventeen outbreaks in 50 years is not a run of bad luck. It is the predictable consequence of structural conditions that have not been addressed with the depth or durability the problem demands. This outbreak is a chance, again, to address them differently, and to finally break the pattern.
